messages.author: 032df22a0c0d5e56
messages.subject: Incomplete b-allele plots by Titan
parts:
Hi,

I have noticed that Titan is unable to plot the b-allele distributions for several chromosomes, in two of my paired samples so far. I have attached a sample error log file. These are all hg19 bams and other samples from the same sequencing run have been processed by Titan just fine. In this case (for the attached sample), Chromosome 16 onwards b-allele plots are missing from all clusters (1 to 5). I am curious as to why the tool is unable to plot the b-allele fractions yet is able to predict copy number events on these chromosomes (Deletions, NLOH, as well as gains).
Any ideas what might be causing this?

Thanks!
Jasleen.

messages.author: 71cefeaaa3659875
messages.subject: Re: Incomplete b-allele plots by Titan
parts:
Hi Jasleen,

1) Can you please indicate the version of TitanCNA you are using?

2) The error you have attached seems to fail when plotting the log ratios and has not made it to the allele ratios.

Error in plot.window(...) : invalid 'xlim' value
Calls: plotCNlogRByChr ... plot -> plot -> plot.default -> localWindow -> plot.window
Execution halted

The plotting function uses the positions in the chromosome to find the size of the chromosome in plotCNlogRByChr
xlim <- as.numeric(c(1, dataByChr[nrow(dataByChr), "Position"]))
It is failing there.  This could mean that there are no data or the data is not read properly for dataByChr.  

You may want to load the R image file to check this.
load(obj_file)

Alternatively, you can look in the segment (*segs.txt) or titan (*titan.txt) output files to see if chr16 is there.

Please let me know what you find.

Best,
Gavin

messages.author: 032df22a0c0d5e56
messages.subject: Re: Incomplete b-allele plots by Titan
parts:
Hi Gavin,
So I have checked the *segs.txt and *titan.txt and all the chromosomes have some or the other copy event called in them (including Chromosome 16). Unfortunately I am using TItanRunner so I am unable to access the temp files created during the plotting (i.e. the R image file).
Here are the specifics of the versions:
TitanRunner v0.1.0 (Created on March 27, 2014).
TitanCNA v1.4.0 (Dated 2014-08-07)

However, I reran these samples this evening, assuming perhaps there had been some memory glitch while these jobs were running on the cluster. Things seem to have worked out now and I see the b-allele plots for all the chromosomes. I am running this on genesis. Based on this, do you think this might have something to do with the queue manager rather than TitanCNA instead? It would be good to know so that this does not happen in the future.

Best,
Jasleen.
